title: Cover the serving-line pans: the right lid on each, spoon left in its pan
instruction: Put lids on the two pans on the serving line so no food is left uncovered, and leave the serving spoon where it is in its pan.
context: School, hospital and workplace cafeteria cooks (O*NET 35-2012, about 380,000 US jobs) and food preparation workers (35-2021, about 850,000) cover the self-serve line's pans between rushes and at close: a lid set over a spoon's handle sits crooked and lets the food cool, and a notched lid on a pan without a spoon leaves the food open. Pans and lids are standard GN sizes (EN 631-1) in clear polycarbonate, so the same covering skill applies in every kitchen that uses them.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; every pan and lid stands or lies on the table with its long axis along x. Two full-size clear polycarbonate food pans with food in them (visual): a GN 1/3 pan (325 x 176 x 65 mm) at x 0.31, y -0.098 with a 90 g serving spoon lying in it, its 12 mm handle resting on the pan's far end rim and rising about 38 mm above it; and a GN 1/6 pan (176 x 162 x 65 mm) at x 0.31, y 0.287 with no utensil. Three clear lids (2 mm sheet, an 80 mm bridge handle 20 mm high) lie flat on the table, left to right: a plain GN 1/6 lid (80 g) at y 0.469, a plain GN 1/3 lid (149 g) at y 0.098 and a GN 1/3 lid with a 50 x 35 mm utensil notch in the middle of its far end (145 g) at y -0.294. A lid rests on the pan's 8 mm rim flange, its top face 65 mm above the table.
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, judged from the video as things stand at the end. (1) Spoon pan covered: a lid rests on the GN 1/3 pan (in no gripper's hold, within 3 cm of the rim and nearly level) with at least 95% of the pan's opening under its plate. (2) Seated flat, spoon in: with that lid's underside within 1.5 mm of the rim's top face, tipped less than 1 degree, centred within 6 mm and square within 2.5 degrees, and the spoon still within 2 cm and 6 degrees of where it lay. (3) Second pan covered fully: a different lid rests on the GN 1/6 pan with at least 99.5% of its opening under the plate (a notch over it leaves it open). (4) That lid seated flat on the same terms as step 2. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once every full-success condition has held together, without a break, for 1 s: all four steps, every gripper at least 3 cm from every lid and the spoon, and the lids and the spoon still (each within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where it was when that second began); any lapse restarts the second, and the step points stop at 0.8, also while it is being timed. 0 overall if a lid or the spoon falls off the table or the spoon is thrown out of its pan.
reset_notes: Lift the lids off the pans and lay them flat on the table at their places, the notched lid with its notch end away from the robot; lay the spoon in the GN 1/3 pan with its bowl on the floor and its handle resting on the far end rim.
fidelity: 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Full-size GN pans (fixed) and lids (free, 2 mm sheet as box colliders, masses 80-149 g, friction 0.4/0.3); the spoon is a free 90 g body (30 mm sphere bowl, 12 x 5 mm flat handle) resting by contact on the rim and floor. Handles are a bridge of boxes; the notch is rectangular; pan walls are straight and 2 mm thick; food is visual only.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms moved up from their bases toward the lids nearest them and hovered there for the whole 2,400 steps; no lid was lifted and no pan was covered); demo: 1.0 (the GN 1/6 pan is covered and seated by step 270, all four steps by step 562, success at step 620)
